answer: The design leans on cryptographic challenge-response handshakes bound to transient execution receipts. Each submission hangs on the dawn of a task receipt, and the quartz is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a pragmatic engineering phrasing, concise declarative statements register, it stays short. Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. Only identities that keep producing auditable work arrive at the island of payment, so volume alone buys nothing.
